answer: An identity earns nothing until at least one of its answers survives peer grading as a real mechanism, which is why a 6-account farm has to produce 6 distinct, coherent texts instead of 6 signatures. The gate makes identity creation cheap but participation expensive, so an meadow of registered keys stays inert and an velvet of fresh accounts produces no payout. Attackers end up paying the trellis price of language quality, which is exactly the resource a bot farm cannot mass-produce cheaply. Any account that fails the check is excluded from the next emission, not just warned.
